title: Steak Sandwiches
shortDescription: Thin-sliced steak, toasted roll, hall classic
subtitle: Thin-sliced steak, toasted roll, hall classic
description: Grill marks, melted cheese, sandwich line. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Season and temper the steak
steps.instruction: Pat sirloin or flank steaks dry; salt and pepper generously. Let sit at room temperature 20 minutes while ovens and grill heat — cold centers overcook the exterior before the middle warms.

steps.title: Roast the vegetables
steps.instruction: Toss bell peppers and zucchini with olive oil, salt, and minced garlic. Spread on sheet pans; roast at 425°F 22 minutes until charred edges show and centers are tender. Hold warm in foil.

steps.title: Grill steak to temp
steps.instruction: Grill over high heat (450°F surface) 3–5 minutes per side until 130–140°F for medium — flank needs a hard sear then brief finish; sirloin takes even heat. Rest 8 minutes tented with foil.

steps.title: Slice against the grain
steps.instruction: Slice rested steak thin at a sharp angle against the grain — short muscle fibers, not long chewy lines. Hold loosely covered at 140°F in a hotel pan with a spoon of butter melted over top.

steps.title: Bake garlic fries
steps.instruction: Spread frozen fries in a single layer. Bake at 425°F 20–22 minutes until crisp; toss hot fries with melted butter and minced garlic. Season with salt immediately; hold in a warm pan.

steps.title: Sauté onions and mushrooms
steps.instruction: Cook sliced onions over medium-high until golden, then add mushrooms until browned and moisture evaporates. Hold warm for the toppings bar with a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Build Caesar and horseradish aioli
steps.instruction: Toss romaine with Caesar dressing, croutons, and parmesan — dress lightly so leaves stay crisp. Whisk horseradish into mayonnaise for aioli; keep both cold on ice until service.

steps.title: Toast buns and melt provolone
steps.instruction: Split sub rolls and toast cut-side down until golden. Pile sliced steak on toasted bottoms, lay provolone over top, and broil 1–2 minutes until cheese laces the edges. Finish with onions, mushrooms, and aioli.

steps.title: Run the toppings bar
steps.instruction: Set steak sandwiches, garlic fries, Caesar salad, roasted vegetables, onions, mushrooms, aioli, and extra provolone in a row. Crew builds their own stack — hot steak center, cold Caesar at the far end.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover sliced steak — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool sliced steak and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Slice steak thin after the rest — crew eats better and portions stretch.
Toast buns hard enough to hold juice without falling apart.
Keep Caesar and aioli on ice until the line opens.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Log hold times on the pan with a grease pencil when tones drop mid-service.
Spot-check proteins with an instant-read thermometer before reopening the line after a call.

whyCrewsLikeIt: Thin-sliced steak, toasted roll, hall classic. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
